title: How do you win the pebble game when you play second?
description: Sanju and Mira play a pebble game on a train. The video tries small piles, finds the copying plan called the mirror strategy, and uses it on two piles of seven.
teaching_notes: One idea: after each move of the first player, copy it on the other pile so the piles stay equal. Watch for the slip of taking a different number from the other pile.

video_script.why: The child can play the game but has not found a plan that always wins for the second player.
video_script.substitution: Try piles of one and two first, then copy every move on the other pile so that the piles stay equal.
video_script.anchor: Sanju and Mira with two heaps of pebbles on the table of a train compartment
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu takes one pebble from the other pile, which leaves 4 and 6; the first player takes 2 from the pile of 6 and now holds the equal piles.

final_answer.value: Take the same number from the other pile; the second player wins
final_answer.spoken: take the same number from the other pile, and the second player wins

never_show: the your-turn answer, take 5 from the other pile
maths_rules: start 7 and 7; the first player takes 3 from one pile, leaving 4 and 7
mirror: take 3 from the other pile, leaving 4 and 4 (equal)
if the first player takes 4 from a pile, take 4 from the other: 0 and 0, and you take the last pebble
equal piles after each move of yours, so the second player takes the last pebble and wins
slip: take 1 from the 7, leaving 4 and 6; the first player takes 2 from 6, leaving 4 and 4

your turn: 9 and 9, the first player takes 5, leaving 4 and 9; take 5 from the other pile; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: copy the move on the other pile. Wrong idea: take a different number. Two piles of pebbles stay on the stage and the piles are updated at every move.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='train'/>Sanju and Mira play a pebble game on the train.
<bookmark mark='piles'/>There are two piles, with seven pebbles in each.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Players take turns, and each takes as many as they like from one pile.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The player who takes the last pebble from either pile wins the game.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>You play second. The first player takes three from one pile. What do you do, and who wins?

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Try small piles first, and with one pebble in each pile, the first player picks one pebble.
<bookmark mark='one_b'/>You pick the other pebble, and you win the game.
<bookmark mark='two'/>With two in each pile, the first player may take both from one pile.
<bookmark mark='two_b'/>You take both from the other pile, and you win again.
<bookmark mark='copy'/>Copying the move on the other pile is called a mirror strategy.
